chunks: Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur narrated from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who wishes to attend to a need while he is in salat (prayer), he عليه السلام said: “He gestures with his head and signals with his hand; and a woman, when she wishes to attend to a need, claps.”

key_terms.بِرَأْسِهِ: with his head, as a restrained form of signaling
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act of worship being discussed
key_terms.ٱلْحَاجَةَ: a need requiring attention or indication
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْأَةُ: the woman, for whom a distinct manner is mentioned

ai.seo_question: How should someone indicate a need while remaining in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about how a person in salat (prayer) may communicate a need without invalidating the prayer. It distinguishes between the manner of indication for a man and a woman, showing brief, minimal gestures are used when necessary during worship.
